title: Base cases for copying joined fields
statement: For every type $\Gamma$, natural number $m\le 1$, there is a natural-number constant $C$ such that for every input word $x$, list of words $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ over $\Gamma$, and starting configuration $d$ of the specified two-tape machine, the following holds. If the machine starts in its designated entry state, tape 0 stores the joined fields throughout offsets $-1$ through their length $L$, and tape 1 is blank throughout those offsets, then it reaches its exit state at some time $t\le C(L+1)$, avoiding that state at every earlier time; both heads stay within distance $C(L+1)$ of their initial positions up to and including time $t$, and at time $t$ tape 1 stores the joined fields in the interval of length $L$ beginning at its initial head position, with all other tape contents and configuration data unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Initial state is the designated copy entry state
Tape 0 satisfies the joined-fields record condition on offsets $-1$ through $L$
Tape 1 is blank on offsets $-1$ through $L$
